div.head: Appendix 200
div.p: Memorandum From American Delegates [Regarding] Trade Between German-Austria and Hungary

The question is presented by recent developments at Vienna as to whether absolutely all trade between Austria and Hungary should be prohibited or whether the Inter-Allied Commission at Vienna should be authorised, in its discretion, to permit such trade across the Austro-Hungarian frontier as may be considered essential to the economic life and political stability of German Austria.

The American Delegation is advised by its representative on the Inter-Allied Commission at Vienna that on instructions from the French Foreign Office the Commission, without the concurrence of the American Delegate, had notified the Austrian Government that all trade between Austria and Hungary was absolutely prohibited, including the export of indigenous as well as imported commodities. In response to this notification a representative of the Austrian Foreign Office appeared before the Commission and stated that if the Commission’s
prohibition was carried into effect it would be most disastrous to Austria. He stated in particular that Vienna was dependent upon certain coal mines in Hungary for operating the electric power and light stations of the city, and that no coal could be got from this source unless Austria exported a small amount of coke to be used in operating the mines. He further stated that Austria must continue certain exports to Hungary in order to obtain agricultural products and provisions.
